gradingPolicy: 3 means excerpt gives relevant original words at an AI-assessed level while retaining scope cautions; 2 means useful context but original-work and/or uncertainty caveat prevents standalone historical-answer treatment. Neither grade is an independent doctrinal editorial approval.
answerPolicy: All displayed Patristic words must come verbatim from the validated canonical chapter loader; do not synthesize a Father reply; the modern question is editorial navigation only. Negative probes ask for unsupported direct claims, not necessarily total suppression of all related original-source navigation.

rows.editorialQuestion: Why does Jesus seem to pass by the frightened disciples?
rows.editorialScope: Augustine interprets the purpose of the apparent passing-by; the Gospel event must not be embellished.
rows.negativeProbe: Did Jesus abandon His disciples and only return after they begged?

rows.editorialQuestion: How can wealthy people enter the kingdom if riches endanger salvation?
rows.editorialScope: The answer concerns detachment and conversion, with distinct camel/Christ typology; fuller Latin names Zacchaeus, missing from Catena.
rows.negativeProbe: Does Bede say that simply owning any wealth necessarily damns a person?

rows.editorialQuestion: What does the angel seated on the right signify?
rows.editorialScope: Gregory explains the right hand of the tomb by a symbolism of everlasting life.
rows.negativeProbe: Does Gregory prove that the angel literally sat at the right hand of God?

rows.editorialQuestion: How can Mark call an appearance of the risen Christ the last?
rows.editorialScope: The Catena extract presents alternatives, but fuller Augustine III.25 §§77 and 83 favors a final pre-Ascension appearance; neither is independent historical proof.
rows.negativeProbe: Did Augustine finally conclude that Mark's last appearance definitely occurred on the resurrection evening?

rows.editorialQuestion: Why did Peter falter after acknowledging Jesus as Christ?
rows.editorialScope: Chrysostom distinguishes Father's revelation of divine Sonship from Peter's then-limited understanding of the Passion.
rows.negativeProbe: Did Peter understand the mystery of the Passion completely when he confessed Christ?

rows.editorialQuestion: Why did Christ curse the fig tree when the season of figs had not arrived?
rows.editorialScope: Chrysostom treats the action as a sign of Christ's freely restrained power and preparation of the disciples for the Passion.
rows.negativeProbe: Does Chrysostom teach that Christ punished the fig tree for being morally guilty?

rows.editorialQuestion: Why does Christ say 'if possible' about deceiving the elect?
rows.editorialScope: Gregory explains the conditional as the elect's trembling under temptation while persevering; no personal election diagnosis follows.
rows.negativeProbe: Can we determine from Gregory's words that a named individual is certainly elect?

rows.editorialQuestion: Why does the Last Supper depict reclining if the Passover required standing?
rows.editorialScope: Theophylact proposes a probable sequence, not a demonstrable reconstruction; a reliable Greek edition remains uninspected.
rows.negativeProbe: Did Theophylact establish as historical fact that Christ held two separate Passover meals?

rows.editorialQuestion: How does Augustine reconcile the two thieves reviling Christ with Luke's account of one repentant thief?
rows.editorialScope: Augustine argues plural-for-singular; the next Catena fragment's 'Or else' alternative cannot be assigned to Augustine automatically.
rows.negativeProbe: Did Augustine personally argue in this extract that both thieves first reviled Christ before one repented?

rows.editorialQuestion: Why identify Judas by his origin or name?
rows.editorialScope: Chrysostom notes how the evangelist distinguishes two Judases without applying a defamatory epithet.
rows.negativeProbe: Did Chrysostom say the evangelist deliberately gave Judas the epithet 'the traitor'?
